I would say do it if your hardware can do it. Assuming you are using YouTube, when you choose a higher quality, even one above your native display resolution, it increases the bitrate of the video. This makes the pixels look much clearer as there is more information supplied to the video stream. If you ever look at a video with a lot of movement on low quality, the moving areas will generally be more blurry, as the player is trying to make assumptions based on previous frames to save bandwidth. If there is more information supplied, the player makes less assumptions, as it knows more about the pixel location, movement, and coloration, and can show you a more clear picture. I choose resolutions above my native display all the time for this reason, so long as my interwebz have enough bandwidth to support it.
